instrument.completeness_rule: the serializer writes EVERY non-const, non-derivable member of GaitWalker's private state; the restore() writes all of it back; a round-trip check re-serializes after restore and requires BYTE-IDENTITY with the dump (the snapshot is complete or the proof fails loudly)
instrument.format: little-endian raw doubles/uint64s, field order fixed by the serializer; header = magic 'CHSNAP01' + format version + tick + n/npts/nd counts + sha256 of the serialized body; a field manifest (name, class, offset, count) ships beside every dump

proof_protocol.mid_walk_tick: T = 150, DERIVED not chosen (Rule 1): the shipped walk refuses at tick ~300-304 (the wave-32 receipt's own tick-300 face; wave-45/47 measure 302), so the future half carries >=150 comparable ticks; 150 lies strictly after the entry transient and the first full exchange era (the R hind fire at 98, its TD replant at 107 on the shipped grid), and INSIDE the post-exchange ride/hold era [107,152) -- literally a mid-hold tick on the shipped calendar; the tick is frozen BEFORE any run
proof_protocol.reference: instrument exe, dump mode: reset + configure(capture_enabled) exactly like the ship harness's walk leg; per tick record the state hash (sha256 of the canonical serialization) and the action bytes (last_torque_, 18 x f64 LE); at the END of tick T write the snapshot + manifest
proof_protocol.restore: FRESH process: rebuild the walker on the same scene, step blind to T, require the blind state hash to equal the reference's H[T] (else F4 territory), restore() the snapshot, round-trip-verify (re-serialize == dump bytes), then continue to the refusal recording hashes + actions
proof_protocol.comparison: the restored future (ticks T+1..refusal) must equal the reference tick-for-tick on BOTH instruments (state hashes, action bytes) and refuse at the same tick with the same class; the restored tick-T hash must equal H[T]
